problems.title: Does P equal NP?
problems.summary: If a computer can quickly check a solution, can it always find one quickly? A schedule that meets every constraint can be easy to verify even when finding it seems hard.
problems.context: P versus NP asks whether every decision problem with polynomial-time verifiable yes-certificates can also be decided in polynomial time. Boolean satisfiability (SAT) is NP-complete. A polynomial-time decision algorithm for every SAT input would prove P = NP. One known special case gives us a place to test where a fast method stops working.
problems.task: Reproduce the fast matching method for clauses with three distinct variables and at most three appearances per variable. The starter gives a four-clause formula where distinct matching fails. Extend the method so that one true literal can serve two clauses, then test your rule against exhaustive truth tables.
problems.review: State exactly which formulas your rule handles. For every claimed solution, give an assignment that a second checker can verify. Show the smallest formula you found that defeats a broader claim, specify the search range, and explain why the example defeats that rule.

sources.title: Clay Mathematics Institute, P versus NP

starter.title: Reproduce the SAT matching proof and test its limit

problems.title: Does every Collatz sequence reach 1?
problems.summary: Pick a positive whole number. If it is even, halve it. If it is odd, triple it and add one. Does every starting number eventually reach 1?
problems.context: A proof that every starting number above 1 eventually drops below itself would settle the conjecture by induction. The starter uses exact algebra to prove this descent for whole families of numbers at once. Terence Tao proved an almost-all result. The conjecture asks about every positive integer.
problems.task: Start with numbers that leave remainder 27 when divided by 4,096. The starter’s 12-step check leaves this family unresolved. Split it into smaller classes and prove that every member of one subclass eventually drops below its starting value. Record the siblings still uncovered.
problems.review: Give the residue and modulus, the odd and even steps, and the exact formula for the resulting value. Check the parity at each step and prove strict descent for every starting number above 1 in the claimed class. Report how much previously uncovered territory the certificate covers.

sources.title: Terence Tao on almost all Collatz orbits
David Bařina on computational verification of the Collatz problem

starter.title: Check descent for whole families of starting numbers

problems.title: What is dark matter?
problems.summary: Stars and gas near the edge of a spiral galaxy can orbit faster than their visible mass predicts. Measure how much faster in one galaxy, then compare it with a second.
problems.context: Astronomers infer dark matter from its gravity. At the outermost measured radius of galaxy NGC 3198, the observed orbital speed is 149 ± 3 km/s. The model for its stars and gas gives 64.71 km/s at the adopted stellar disk mass-to-light ratio of 0.5 in solar units. The speed difference constrains the gravitational field. The identity of dark matter remains open.
problems.task: Reproduce the NGC 3198 result, then test whether the gap persists in NGC 2403. Use every measured radius at or beyond half the last measured radius. Repeat the calculation at disk mass-to-light ratios of 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8.
problems.review: Use SPARC Table 2 for an independent calculation. Report the galaxy, radial range, number of measurements and median observed minus predicted speed in km/s for each ratio. Check the outermost point by hand and distinguish the measured speed error from model uncertainty.

sources.title: SPARC rotation measurements and Newtonian mass models
Lelli, McGaugh and Schombert on the SPARC mass models
NASA on the evidence for dark matter

starter.title: Reproduce the rotation curve of NGC 3198

problems.title: Can a free browser editor preserve editable layers and masks?
problems.summary: Create a browser editor for everyday photo compositing and retouching, free to use and open to inspect.
problems.context: Photoshop’s layers, masks and blending make a composite editable after it is assembled. This project starts with that workflow in an original browser interface, using files from the person’s device. GIMP is an existing open-source precedent.
problems.task: Build a small prototype that opens two PNGs as layers and lets someone reorder them, adjust opacity and paint a mask. Save a reopenable project and export a transparent PNG. Use original interface code and sample artwork.
problems.review: Supply two redistributable PNGs, a short demo and a pixel comparison for the expected export. Reopening the project preserves the layer order, opacity and mask. The workflow runs locally with no account or subscription.

problems.title: Can a local budget app import two bank CSVs without double-counting?
problems.summary: Turn downloaded bank CSVs into a monthly budget that people can keep on their own device.
problems.context: Monarch combines transaction categorization and monthly planning. This project starts with a local budgeting workflow using file import. Actual Budget already demonstrates open-source budgeting and transaction imports.
problems.task: Prototype a screen for importing CSVs from two accounts. Preview the column mapping, let someone categorize spending, and show a planned-versus-actual monthly view. Use synthetic data and provide a local export.
problems.review: Reimporting the same files keeps totals unchanged. Two real purchases of the same amount remain distinct, transfers cancel without adding to spending, and refunds are handled explicitly. Show the expected totals in integer cents and how a reviewer can reproduce them.

problems.title: Can an offline PDF comparison survive a page insertion?
problems.summary: Build a free tool that shows what changed between two versions of a document on your own device.
problems.context: Acrobat Pro can compare two PDF revisions and produce a report. Existing open-source projects such as diff-pdf demonstrate visual comparison. This project proposes a simple local workflow for matching pages and sharing a review report.
problems.task: Prototype a workflow that accepts two PDFs locally and marks added, removed and changed pages. Export a small report with page references and a visual difference for edited pages.
problems.review: Provide original fixture PDFs with an inserted page, a deleted page and one edit. Confirm that an insertion does not mark every following page as changed, that accessible text labels identify each difference, and that an unchanged pair produces no differences.

problems.title: Has Rockstar announced a PC release for GTA VI?
problems.summary: Track official PC release announcements, dates and system requirements.
problems.context: Rockstar launched GTA VI on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026. Its product page and Take-Two’s launch release listed those platforms on November 26. An official PC date and requirements remained unconfirmed in those sources.
problems.task: Check Rockstar’s product page and Newswire and Take-Two’s release archive. Record the check date, platform, region, release date and requirements exactly as supported by the sources.
problems.review: Provide first-party URLs and announcement dates for changed fields. Mark unavailable fields as unconfirmed and retain prior confirmed entries so a reviewer can check the change.

starter.title: November 26 release check and source ledger

problems.title: Does the sparse permanent algorithm agree with exhaustive counting?
problems.summary: Check a small component of recent work on the Exponential Time Hypothesis against an independent reference.
problems.context: An October 2026 preprint presents a subexponential algorithm for exact k-SAT. November lecture notes explain a route through the permanent of sparse matrices. The proposed experiment concerns correctness on small inputs and practical resource cost.
problems.task: Implement the bounded-degree permanent routine from the notes for small integer matrices, with a fixed bound on the count of nonzero entries in each row and column. Compare with permutation enumeration on empty, diagonal, singular and seeded sparse fixtures.
problems.review: Publish the code and seeded input list. Require exact integer agreement and report wall time and peak memory by matrix size. State the size and degree limits of the run.

problems.title: When does changing 3D anti-aliasing cause stutter in Godot?
problems.summary: Measure whether applying MSAA at startup shifts GPU pipeline work into loading or leaves later first-use hitches.
problems.context: An open Godot issue documents draw-time pipeline compilations after an MSAA change. This is a portable graphics problem that can be tested with a small original scene.
problems.task: In a pinned Forward+ Godot build, run a repeatable camera path past staggered material variants. Compare applying the same MSAA level before loading and after loading. Do at least five runs per condition with documented cold and warm caches.
problems.review: Publish the redistributable scene, engine revision, OS, GPU, driver, renderer settings, raw frame times and compilation counters. Report loading time, p99 frame time and frames over 33.3 ms separately for each run, including runs with no hitch.

starter.title: Frame-trace analysis starter and synthetic sample

problems.title: Which SAT solver finishes more public cases in 60 seconds?
problems.summary: Compare two pinned solvers on 12 predetermined 2026 competition instances under the same single-core limit.
problems.context: SAT Competition 2026 publishes instance-level results, solvers and benchmarks. A small, fixed sample makes it possible for another contributor to reproduce a comparison.
problems.task: Predeclare 12 public instance hashes, two solvers that output checkable witnesses or certificates, and a one-core 60-second wall-time limit. Publish one driver command to run both.
problems.review: For every solver and instance, report the model or certificate check, elapsed time, timeout or error, and environment. Count only independently verified answers as solved.

sources.title: SAT Competition output and certificate rules

starter.title: Pinned twelve-case comparison and checked results

problems.title: What breaks when the same open game runs through Proton?
problems.summary: Compare the same redistributable Windows build on Windows and Proton, with a native Linux build as a reference.
problems.context: Valve’s Proton release notes document launch, controller and frame-pacing fixes. An open game with a fixed scene makes regressions easier to reproduce and share.
problems.task: Choose a redistributable game that exports native Windows and Linux builds from the same source revision. Use a scripted path and fixed inputs to check launch, controller mapping and one streaming transition on all three configurations.
problems.review: Publish versions, build hashes, OS and driver details, a pass or fail for each check and reproducible steps for one difference. Use the same in-engine frame-time definition for cross-platform comparisons.

problems.title: Can we check each direction of the 3-SAT to CLIQUE reduction?
problems.summary: Prove the standard construction and check it against independently enumerated small instances.
problems.context: A clique of size equal to the number of clauses picks one consistent literal from each clause. Repeated literals and contradictions are useful fixtures because they expose mistakes in a graph generator or witness translator.
problems.task: Run the repository’s checker, then add a bounded fixture family with known outcomes or formalize one direction and connect it to the exact graph construction.
problems.review: Include the formula family, expected decision and witness checks. State what the finite run checks and give the general proof for the reduction.

problems.title: Does any language in E^NP require Ω(n log n)-size unrestricted circuits?
problems.summary: Work on a circuit lower-bound question explicitly posed in a November 2026 preprint.
problems.context: The open question concerns languages in deterministic time 2^O(n) with an NP oracle and unrestricted Boolean circuits. In the more restrictive disjunctive normal form model, odd parity requires exponentially many terms.
problems.task: Reproduce the odd-parity lower bound for depth-two disjunctive normal form. Identify the place in the argument that relies on each term being a conjunction of literals.
problems.review: Supply a proof of the bound and an independent small truth-table check. State the circuit model, size measure and which lower-bound claim remains open.

starter.title: Exact parity bound and exhaustive checker

problems.title: Does memory help an agent solve ARC-AGI-3 levels in fewer moves?
problems.summary: Test an agent with and without persistent scratch memory at matched action and inference budgets.
problems.context: ARC Prize publishes interactive environments and human play traces. A paired experiment can show whether retaining observations helps a specific agent on a fixed set of levels.
problems.task: Choose ten public levels before running the experiment. Pin the model and harness and compare memory on and off with matched token and action budgets, using the same starting states and repeat seeds.
problems.review: Publish level IDs, run settings, replay files, completion rates and moves used. Include failed and timed-out runs and report how the moves comparison handles them.

problems.title: How often does a model change its answer when the choices move?
problems.summary: Test how much a model’s answer depends on answer position on a small MMLU-Pro sample.
problems.context: The MMLU-Pro authors test sensitivity to prompt styles. This experiment fixes the question and model and changes only the order of choices.
problems.task: Select 30 public question IDs from one subject before the run. Generate five seeded option orders per question, remap the answer labels, and evaluate one pinned model with a fixed prompt and generation settings.
problems.review: Publish question IDs, permutations, parsed option identities, invalid-answer counts and accuracy by position. Report how often the same question receives different option identities and include an unshuffled control.

problems.title: How should OpenRefine preview a join with duplicate keys?
problems.summary: Make a common data-cleaning operation easier to inspect and repeat.
problems.context: An open OpenRefine proposal asks for a clearer way to join data across projects. Duplicate keys and unmatched rows are where a seemingly simple join can produce misleading results.
problems.task: Create two small CSVs with a duplicate key, a missing match, and fields someone might want to keep. Prototype how a person selects keys and fields and previews the result.
problems.review: Publish the input and expected output. Show how duplicates and unmatched rows are represented and how the choices could be recorded in project history for replay.

problems.title: Can a shared transit feed assign each notice to the right agency?
problems.summary: Help operators see which findings in a shared timetable belong to them.
problems.context: A single GTFS feed can serve more than one operator. A combined validation report makes it harder for each agency to find the notices it can act on. MobilityData is discussing how to attribute notices to agencies.
problems.task: Build a tiny synthetic feed with two agencies and draft the shape of a per-agency report. Include at least one notice that involves the whole feed.
problems.review: Show the fixture and command. The expected report assigns each attributable finding to the right agency and handles feed-wide findings explicitly.

problems.title: Where do Seattle’s mapped routes to transit leave wheelchair access uncertain?
problems.summary: Audit curb ramps, crossings and slopes on a sample of 20 trips between transit stops and public destinations.
problems.context: OpenSidewalks and AccessMap model sidewalk attributes that ordinary shortest-path directions can miss. Missing data can make a crossing’s suitability uncertain.
problems.task: Preselect 20 public stop-to-destination pairs in one neighborhood. Generate routes with a specified accessibility profile, review segments with missing data and record dated public-source or field observations.
problems.review: Publish route GeoJSON, the routing profile and the evidence type for each flagged segment. Tabulate verified barriers, verified passable segments and unknowns. Record the routes that could not be generated.

sources.title: University of Washington’s Taskar Center documentation

problems.title: Can a shared link open a digitized manuscript at the right page?
problems.summary: Open a digitized book at the page someone actually meant to share.
problems.context: IIIF Content State describes a portable way to open an object at a particular place. Mirador tracks support for importing that state. A single-page example is a small, useful piece of the wider proposal.
problems.task: Choose an openly accessible IIIF manifest and create a Content State link for one page. Prototype loading it in a fresh Mirador session.
problems.review: Publish the manifest and target canvas URLs. Show that a new session selects the intended page. Include what happens when the manifest or canvas identifier is invalid.

problems.title: How many OCR errors can we verify in one historic newspaper column?
problems.summary: Correct one column from a public scan and record exactly what changed.
problems.context: The Library of Congress is reprocessing Chronicling America to improve searchable text. Public scans and word-level machine transcriptions make it possible to document improvements page by page.
problems.task: Choose one column on a pre-1920 page. Create a TSV with stable line references, the original OCR, corrected text, and flags for uncertain readings.
problems.review: Link the original scan and machine text. A second reader can compare every line with the source image and identify remaining uncertainty.

problems.title: Which Phoenix neighborhoods stay hottest after sunset?
problems.summary: Compare observed land-surface heat across neighborhoods using public satellite data.
problems.context: NASA’s ECOSTRESS captures land-surface temperature at different times of day. Phoenix has published a tree-canopy study layer. This is a proposed analysis of how nighttime surface temperature and canopy vary across the city.
problems.task: Choose clear scenes that cover Phoenix, document their local acquisition times, and join quality-filtered temperatures to tracts and the public tree-canopy layer.
problems.review: Publish scene IDs, quality masks, a tract-level table, and coverage and missingness. Repeat with a different scene or coverage threshold, and explain how your conclusion depends on the choice.

sources.title: City of Phoenix tree-canopy study layer

problems.title: Could moving a two-hour computing job lower estimated electricity emissions?
problems.summary: Backtest immediate and delayed starts in the same eight-hour window using an hourly California grid series.
problems.context: EIA publishes hourly electricity generation and estimated CO₂ emissions. The Carbon Aware SDK provides an example of workload scheduling around electricity emissions intensity.
problems.task: Choose one month and one California balancing authority. For a constant-power two-hour job released at the same time each day, compare immediate execution with a fixed delay chosen from the previous month. Also calculate the lowest observed emissions window as a hindsight reference.
problems.review: Publish dataset timestamps, missing-hour rules, estimated average emissions intensity of load and calculations. Report results for all complete days, excluded days and deadline misses. Make the accounting basis explicit.

sources.title: EIA hourly electric grid data methodology
Green Software Foundation Carbon Aware SDK

problems.title: Can reviewers agree on which galaxy images show an overlap?
problems.summary: Create a small public benchmark from released catalogs and telescope images.
problems.context: Images of overlapping galaxies are useful for studying dust. Galaxy Zoo has published accepted and rejected candidate catalogs, and the Legacy Surveys provide public image cutouts.
problems.task: Select 20 accepted and 20 rejected coordinates from the released catalogs. Retrieve same-scale cutouts, conceal their source labels, and have two reviewers independently label them overlap, no overlap or uncertain.
problems.review: Publish the selection rule, cutout locations, label rubric, reviewers’ decisions and exclusions. Report inter-reviewer agreement and how often each reviewer agrees with the source labels.

problems.title: Are all rational Hodge classes algebraic?
problems.summary: Identify which topological features of algebraic varieties come from algebraic cycles.
problems.context: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Hodge conjecture as a Millennium Prize Problem. Concrete examples can help distinguish cases where a statement is already known from the general conjecture.
problems.task: Work through a known low-dimensional case or explicit projective example. Identify the relevant rational cohomology class, give a candidate algebraic cycle, and explain how their relationship is checked.
problems.review: Cite the exact theorem used and state its hypotheses. A second reader can follow the calculation, reproduce any computations, and identify the limits of the example.

problems.title: What does the November matrix-multiplication proof check in Lean?
problems.summary: Audit the theorem statement and assumptions behind a new matrix-multiplication preprint.
problems.context: The November 24 authors report an exponent of 9/4. The accompanying Lean scope describes a theorem for division-free circuits computing formal polynomial identities. The scope audit compares the exact formal and manuscript claims.
problems.task: Pin the source and Lean toolchain. Build the named square-exponent theorem, print its statement and axioms, and trace the definitions for formal identities and counted operations.
problems.review: Publish the commit, build and print commands and a comparison of field assumptions, division, identity model and gate metric. Mark any manuscript step that you did not independently check.

problems.title: Can a tiny reference solver check the smallest forest shared by two trees?
problems.summary: Build a brute-force oracle for small rooted trees and compare it with a PACE 2026 exact solver.
problems.context: The PACE 2026 challenge studied maximum agreement forests and published a tiny set, a checker and access to submitted solvers. An independent implementation can check whether an output is minimal on small inputs.
problems.task: Use the published rooted binary tree format. Enumerate candidate edge cuts for inputs with at most eight leaves, compare the resulting forests using their labeled rooted topology, and check the reported optimum with one pinned exact submission.
problems.review: Publish tree pairs, minimum component counts, witness forests and checker output. Include identical trees and a hand-checkable conflicting pair and state which cases fell outside the oracle’s bounds.

problems.title: How much does an AI time-horizon estimate change if one task family is omitted?
problems.summary: Measure the sensitivity of published 50% task-completion time horizons to the mixture of task families.
problems.context: METR publishes data and methods for estimating how long a human would take on tasks that agents can complete with a given probability. Closely related tasks can influence a fitted horizon together.
problems.task: Pin the public TH1.1 scored runs and analysis code. Reproduce the released baseline for two models, then refit after leaving out one task family at a time using the same fit settings.
problems.review: Publish task and run counts, baseline and per-family estimates, and any failed or poorly determined fits. Check the same code reproduces the baseline before interpreting changes.

problems.title: Do five FrontierMath Erdős statements preserve the original mathematical hypotheses?
problems.summary: Compare original problem statements with their Lean formulations before treating a proof as evidence of a solution.
problems.context: Epoch AI released formal statements for a set of Erdős problems. A faithful formalization needs equivalent domains, conditions and quantifiers even when the surface wording changes.
problems.task: Preselect five formalized statements at a pinned revision. Have two reviewers compare each original statement with its Lean definitions, domains, assumptions and quantifiers.
problems.review: Publish the source-to-formal statement mapping, commit, reviewer decisions and a minimal example for any semantic difference. Record disagreements and ambiguous translations.

problems.title: Do both USGS APIs report the same mean daily river discharge?
problems.summary: Compare the legacy WaterServices and modern OGC endpoints across known gauges, dates and pagination.
problems.context: USGS is migrating users from WaterServices to new APIs. A client needs to preserve daily dates, discharge values, units and quality fields when switching endpoints.
problems.task: Reproduce the repository’s fixed three-gauge check, then repeat for a declared week with provisional or missing observations. Follow the modern API’s next links with a small page size.
problems.review: Report missing, duplicate, extra and mismatched gauge-days. Compare dates, exact decimal values and units, and report approval status separately from qualifiers. Attach the query parameters and raw page counts.

starter.title: Live three-gauge comparison and rerunnable check

problems.title: Do GeoParquet exports preserve measures and coordinate systems across tools?
problems.summary: Exercise a measured geometry and its coordinate reference system across DuckDB and GDAL readers and writers.
problems.context: GeoParquet 2.0 can use native Parquet geometry metadata. DuckDB’s spatial project tracks a metadata question for measured M and ZM geometries, which encode a measure in addition to spatial ordinates.
problems.task: Use an original tiny dataset with a measured line, a ZM line and an unmeasured control in an explicit coordinate reference system. Export in GeoParquet 1.x and 2.0 with pinned versions and read each file back in both tools.
problems.review: Publish commands, version and capability matrix, native schema and file metadata, and coordinate and measure comparisons with stated tolerance. Record any unsupported export as such and distinguish it from silently dropped metadata.

problems.title: How closely do satellite and dam-gauge changes agree at Lake Powell?
problems.summary: Compare changes in water-surface elevation from qualifying satellite passes and the public dam-gauge series.
problems.context: NASA’s SWOT LakeSP product reports pass-level water elevations and quality flags. The Bureau of Reclamation releases observed daily Lake Powell elevations. A relative-change comparison can handle an undocumented constant datum offset.
problems.task: Predeclare October 1 through November 20, 2026. Select all qualifying Lake Powell passes with a fixed lake identifier and quality filter. Match each to the nearest daily gauge reading and subtract each series’ first matched value.
problems.review: Include IDs, acquisition dates, time gaps, excluded passes, units and uncertainties. Report relative change in metres and only compare absolute levels if a common vertical datum is documented.

sources.title: Bureau of Reclamation Lake Powell elevation data

problems.title: Which Zarr chunk shape reads fewer bytes for a time series and for a map?
problems.summary: Measure how the same gridded array reads under two chunk shapes and two common scientific queries.
problems.context: Xarray supports Zarr for chunked scientific arrays, and a September release added read support for rectilinear Zarr v3 chunks. This experiment uses regular writable chunk shapes to measure a basic workload trade-off.
problems.task: Write the same deterministic 120×180×360 array twice using 30×15×15 and 1×90×90 chunk shapes. Hold dtype and compression fixed. Read a 90-step point series and an aligned 90×90 single-time slice with fresh caches.
problems.review: Publish source, store configuration, read requests, data and metadata bytes and exact output equality. Report median elapsed time across five runs per workload and disclose the storage backend.

starter.title: Measured local chunk reads and exact equality check

problems.title: Can Audacity’s restored Plot Spectrum find the same peaks as Audacity 3?
problems.summary: Use an original two-tone WAV to compare the spectrum from the restored tool with an Audacity 3 export.
problems.context: Audacity maintainers are working to bring Plot Spectrum to version 4.2. Known input frequencies and amplitudes give both the current and restored analysis tools a checkable reference.
problems.task: Generate the repository’s 48 kHz mono fixture. In Audacity 3 and a 4.2 build with Plot Spectrum, select the same interval, use a Hann window and a 4,096-point spectrum, and export each result.
problems.review: Publish build IDs, settings and the two exports. Check for peaks at 468.75 Hz and 937.5 Hz within one frequency bin and a relative level difference near 12.04 dB within 1 dB.

starter.title: Deterministic two-tone WAV and spectrum checker

problems.title: Does adding stationary keyframes rotate a camera during glTF export?
problems.summary: Compare static and identically keyed camera orientation when Blender exports the same scene to glTF.
problems.context: Blender’s glTF exporter has an open report about animated camera orientation when Y Up is disabled. An independent fixture can check the reported behavior and the proposed change.
problems.task: Build an original asymmetric scene with a rotated camera. Export it once statically and once with two identical rotation keys, with Y Up disabled and enabled. Test a stable exporter and the candidate revision.
problems.review: Publish the scene, export settings, revisions and decoded static and keyed world rotations. Account for quaternion sign equivalence and measure the angular difference in degrees.

problems.title: Does a texture finish sharpening after the Godot camera stops moving?
problems.summary: Compare texture streaming with continuous redraw and with low-processor mode after a camera move stops.
problems.context: An issue on Godot’s 4.8 milestone concerns texture streaming and redraw in low-processor mode. A small original scene makes it possible to compare visible output without shipping game assets.
problems.task: Use an original mipmapped checkerboard on one plane. Move from a distant camera pose to a fixed near pose and record the same region at fixed times. Compare low-processor and continuous redraw, plus a full-resolution reference.
problems.review: Publish the engine build, GPU, driver, rendering settings, image crops and a declared image-similarity threshold. Report time to match the reference and whether a forced redraw changes the result.

problems.title: Can a launcher read the real game exit status through Gamescope?
problems.summary: Exercise normal exits, errors and missing commands in a small headless and Wayland comparison.
problems.context: Gamescope has a reported child-process status issue and a proposed change. An exit-code fixture can check that launchers can distinguish deliberate game exit from failure.
problems.task: Use harmless local dummy commands for exits 0 and 7, self-SIGTERM and a missing program. Compare a stable build and the proposed change headlessly and under nested Wayland.
problems.review: Publish expected and observed exit codes for both builds and backends with tool versions. Cover an explicit compositor shutdown separately and record unavailable test configurations.

problems.title: Can an archived page’s Load More button replay results from the same capture date?
problems.summary: Check that a page and its paginated results stay associated when replaying two archived snapshots.
problems.context: Webrecorder’s pywb project tracks a date-selection issue involving archived POST responses. An original local page and two archived snapshots can isolate the date-matching behavior.
problems.task: Create a local page with two POST pagination requests and archive captures at two timestamps with different visible markers per page. Stop the original server and replay each capture, testing JSON and form-encoded bodies.
problems.review: Publish redistributable inputs, pywb version and request logs. Each replay must show its two markers in order and all successful pagination responses must come from the matching capture.

problems.title: Why does a simulated Nav2 controller slow down on long waypoint lists?
problems.summary: Isolate how the cost of pruning and reporting a path scales with the number of remaining waypoints.
problems.context: A Nav2 issue reports per-cycle work growing with path length even when the controller plugin stays fixed. The report measured an x86 system and requests more evidence about smaller processors.
problems.task: Drive the same path-handler and remaining-length functions with deterministic virtual routes of 10,000, 100,000 and 400,000 poses. Hold advancing distance and plugin settings fixed and measure components separately.
problems.review: Publish generator, versions, architecture and median and p95 timings across repeated runs. Include remaining-distance and path-segment comparisons if evaluating a proposed optimization.

problems.title: Does Gazebo report a scripted actor at its actual simulated position?
problems.summary: Compare a scripted actor’s reported world pose with a known linear trajectory.
problems.context: An open Gazebo Sim report says Actor::WorldPose can return the base pose for an actor following a scripted trajectory. A headless fixture with a short straight route offers a checkable expectation.
problems.task: Use Gazebo’s documented actor trajectory pattern with a nonzero base translation and a straight scripted segment. Log world pose in a defined update phase at three known simulation times, plus a stationary control.
problems.review: Publish the original world, simulation version, step size and logged versus expected poses. Distinguish base pose and trajectory coordinates and report any sampling offset.

sources.title: Gazebo Sim actor world pose issue #4131

problems.title: When does a MuJoCo box-on-edge contact collapse to one point?
problems.summary: Check how small changes in box angle affect the reported virtual contact manifold.
problems.context: An open MuJoCo report shows one contact near the end of an overlapping box edge. Comparing nearby angles and a flat-face control can help characterize where the reported contact pattern changes.
problems.task: Construct two original virtual boxes with dimensions and poses documented in the report. Evaluate contacts at the reported pose, nearby angular perturbations and one simple no-contact control using a pinned engine.
problems.review: Publish the model and angles, engine version, distances and individual contact positions in world coordinates. Show controls and distinguish static contact reports from claims about motion over time.

starter.title: Two-box model, angle sweep and measured contacts
